key_insight: Homogeneous WC–Co–Cr powder produces dense layered coatings, while spray method controls the tradeoff between hardness and tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: The study helps select HVOF or detonation spraying to optimize wear-resistant coatings for machine parts operating under high friction and load.
method: Compared WC–Co–Cr coatings made by detonation spraying and HVOF
Characterized powder, microstructure, and phase composition using SEM and EDS
Measured coating hardness, density, and friction behavior
evidence_signal: Detonation spraying achieved higher average microhardness (1449 HV), while HVOF produced a dense, uniform coating with a low friction coefficient (Kt = 0.143).
watch_item: Results depend strongly on powder morphology and process conditions, so the same coating performance may not transfer without careful parameter control.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
